text:
kevin: Heads-up — I sketched a small playbook for transient GPU node handshakes to reduce churn when preemptions or short control-plane/network blips happen. Goal: avoid useless scale-up/down loops and give pods a chance to migrate cleanly.

maria_g: quick Q — can we do this without changing instance templates/ASGs? trying to avoid infra churn.

kevin: yes, most of it is k8s-level. high level: 1) termination/webhook annotates node with `transient/handshake=1` 2) add a taint `transient/preempting:NoSchedule` and a toleration for critical runtime pods 3) signal CA to treat annotated nodes as "ignore for 60s" 4) daemonset warms replacement nodes (small GPU warmers) and marks them Ready once warmed.

jon: prototype flow I tried yesterday: on preempt notice -> annotate -> patch node with taint -> run `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` for non-critical pods -> keep critical pods on node with toleration. If replacement not Ready within 90s, escalate to on-demand pool.

leah: curious about CA integration. CA supports `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable` and `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled`. Could we leverage `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/ignore=true` on annotated nodes for a short window to stop scale-down race?

kevin: exactly. snippet I put in the prototype controller: 

```
# mark node during handshake
kubectl annotate node $NODE transient/handshake=1 --overwrite
kubectl taint node $NODE transient/preempting=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
# set CA annotation so it won't immediately re-evaluate
kubectl annotate node $NODE cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/ignore=true --overwrite
# controller will remove annotations/taints after 60s or when replacement Ready
```

samira: we should add a network-awareness hook — last week we saw control-plane packet loss for ~40s in eu-west-1 and CA started killing nodes while new ones were still initializing. If handshake respects a network probe (curl control-plane:443) -> extend handshake to 90s, maybe fewer thrashes.

kevin: good point. add a small probe in the webhook: if control-plane connectivity unstable, extend `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/ignore` TTL to 120s.

infra-ci-bot: ci:node-handshake-tests pipeline started for branch `kevin/transient-handshake` — smoke + e2e for drain behavior + CA annotations. (job 4521)

maria_g: :thumbsup: I'll review the taint/annotation names. Suggest we standardize on `transient/preempting` and `transient/handshake-ttl` annotation (seconds). Also add metric `infra.transient.handshakes` to console so ops can correlate with cost spikes.

jon: another operational note — add a fallback policy: if replacement node not Ready in Xs (configurable, default 90s), automatically trigger scale action to on-demand pool and annotate affected pods with `migration=forced`. That gave us predictable cost but avoided application errors.

kevin: plan: I'll open a short PR with controller + webhook + CA annotation change + docs (ops playbook). @maria_g can you review taint/annotation names? @samira please outline the network-probe extension behavior. Will add the metric to console after PR.

maria_g: on it, will post review comments today.

leah: also add a runbook snippet: when handshake failures > 5/min, disable transient pool for the region and pivot traffic to dedicated capacity.

kevin: perfect. I'll add that to the runbook and flag for a small canary test in staging.

samira: leaving a reminder — include explicit test for mixed-capacity scheduling (spot + on-demand) to ensure tolerations behave as expected.

kevin: acknowledged. thanks all. I'll track in the PR and tag this thread. :white_check_mark:
